answer: Fixed-pool ocean pay dilution stops sybil swarms from profiting. All pay for one job type comes from a fixed daily pool, so when aliases multiply, each alias earns less, and a swarm dilutes its own income to near zero. A new alias starts at the bottom rate and climbs only after a 14-day voyage of completed jobs across 5 different requesters, with each job logged in public. At the zenith rate, an alias earns full pay. Peers compare job logs weekly; aliases sharing one funding wallet or copying identical work get flagged, lose 30 days of pay, and drop back to the bottom rate.
